verses.pali: Okkācitavinītā parisā nopaṭipucchāvinītā, paṭipucchāvinītā parisā nookkācitavinītā.
verses.english: An assembly educated in fancy talk, not in questioning, and an assembly educated in questioning, not in fancy talk.

verses.pali: Katamā ca, bhikkhave, okkācitavinītā parisā nopaṭipucchāvinītā?
verses.english: And what is an assembly educated in fancy talk, not in questioning?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, yassaṁ parisāyaṁ bhikkhū ye te suttantā tathāgatabhāsitā gambhīrā gambhīratthā lokuttarā suññatāpaṭisaṁyuttā tesu bhaññamānesu na sussūsanti na sotaṁ odahanti na aññā cittaṁ upaṭṭhapenti na ca te dhamme uggahetabbaṁ pariyāpuṇitabbaṁ maññanti.
verses.english: It is an assembly where, when discourses spoken by the Realized One—deep, profound, transcendent, dealing with emptiness—are being recited the mendicants do not want to listen. They don’t actively listen or try to understand, nor do they think those teachings are worth learning and memorizing.

verses.pali: Ye pana te suttantā kavitā kāveyyā cittakkharā cittabyañjanā bāhirakā sāvakabhāsitā tesu bhaññamānesu sussūsanti sotaṁ odahanti aññā cittaṁ upaṭṭhapenti, te dhamme uggahetabbaṁ pariyāpuṇitabbaṁ maññanti, te ca taṁ dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇitvā na ceva aññamaññaṁ paṭipucchanti na ca paṭivicaranti:
verses.english: But when discourses composed by poets—poetry, with fancy words and phrases, composed by outsiders or spoken by disciples—are being recited the mendicants do want to listen. They actively listen and try to understand, and they think those teachings are worth learning and memorizing. But when they’ve memorized those teachings they don’t question or examine each other, saying:
‘Why does it say this? What does that mean?’

verses.pali: Te avivaṭañceva na vivaranti, anuttānīkatañca na uttānīkaronti, anekavihitesu ca kaṅkhāṭhāniyesu dhammesu kaṅkhaṁ na paṭivinodenti.
verses.english: So they don’t reveal what is hidden or clarify what is unclear, or dispel doubt regarding the many doubtful matters.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, okkācitavinītā parisā no paṭipucchāvinītā.
verses.english: This is called an assembly educated in fancy talk, not in questioning.

verses.pali: Katamā ca, bhikkhave, paṭipucchāvinītā parisā nookkācitavinītā?
verses.english: And what is an assembly educated in questioning, not in fancy talk?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, yassaṁ parisāyaṁ bhikkhū ye te suttantā kavitā kāveyyā cittakkharā cittabyañjanā bāhirakā sāvakabhāsitā tesu bhaññamānesu na sussūsanti na sotaṁ odahanti na aññā cittaṁ upaṭṭhapenti, na ca te dhamme uggahetabbaṁ pariyāpuṇitabbaṁ maññanti.
verses.english: It is an assembly where, when discourses composed by poets—poetry, with fancy words and phrases, composed by outsiders or spoken by disciples—are being recited the mendicants do not want to listen. They don’t actively listen or try to understand, nor do they think those teachings are worth learning and memorizing.

verses.pali: Ye pana te suttantā tathāgatabhāsitā gambhīrā gambhīratthā lokuttarā suññatāpaṭisaṁyuttā tesu bhaññamānesu sussūsanti sotaṁ odahanti aññā cittaṁ upaṭṭhapenti, te ca dhamme uggahetabbaṁ pariyāpuṇitabbaṁ maññanti.
verses.english: But when discourses spoken by the Realized One—deep, profound, transcendent, dealing with emptiness—are being recited the mendicants do want to listen. They actively listen and try to understand, and they think those teachings are worth learning and memorizing.

verses.pali: Te taṁ dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇitvā aññamaññaṁ paṭipucchanti paṭivicaranti:
verses.english: And when they’ve memorized those teachings they question and examine each other, saying:
‘Why does it say this? What does that mean?’

verses.pali: Te avivaṭañceva vivaranti, anuttānīkatañca uttānīkaronti, anekavihitesu ca kaṅkhāṭhāniyesu dhammesu kaṅkhaṁ paṭivinodenti.
verses.english: So they reveal what is hidden, clarify what is unclear, and dispel doubt regarding the many doubtful matters.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, paṭipucchāvinītā parisā nookkācitavinītā.
verses.english: This is called an assembly educated in questioning, not in fancy talk.

verses.pali: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imāsaṁ dvinnaṁ parisānaṁ yadidaṁ paṭipucchāvinītā parisā nookkācitavinītā”ti.
verses.english: The better of these two assemblies is the assembly educated in questioning, not in fancy talk.”
